narrative_markdown:
## Today's Forecast

Evening clouds dominate as the day moves toward a Mostly cloudy sky. Thunder possible from the morning, peaking this evening, and showers are expected to begin between 18:00 and 19:00, delivering about 6.5 mm (0.26 in) of rain. The wind shifts from a north-northeasterly overnight to a southwest by midday, with gusts up to 32 km/h (17 kt) ashore. UV reaches a peak index of 9.2. Air quality is estimated at AQI 86, while ground stations report the best reading of AQI 54 at Ochieng' Avenue. As of 06:01, reports through 03:00: no rain; no thunder; high so far 21°C (70°F); low so far 20°C (68°F); peak sustained 9 km/h (5 kt); sky partly cloudy.

## Extended Outlook

Next three days will see temperatures and winds much the same through Sunday, with showers possible Friday and Saturday, dry Sunday, and thunderstorms likely each day. Friday’s sky is Mostly cloudy, Saturday Mostly cloudy, Sunday Mostly cloudy. Rain chances rise to 54 % on Sunday, with highs between 30°C (86°F) and 31°C (88°F) and lows near 19°C (66°F). The Day+3 call gives a 54 % rain probability, while the Day+7 call predicts rain with 100 % certainty. Records note no extreme temperature breaches for these periods.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential

Peak CAPE values of 1550 J/kg (Best Match), 1570 J/kg (ICON) and 4180 J/kg (UKMO) signal thunderstorm potential, especially at the 18:00 peak. This could bring sudden gusts well above the forecast 32 km/h (17 kt), so be prepared for brief, stronger wind bursts. No formal warning bulletin has been issued by the Kenya Meteorological Department.

## Winam Gulf — Conditions for Boaters

Over Winam Gulf the wind is northeasterly overnight at 7 km/h (4 kt), gusting 11 km/h (6 kt), then shifts to south-southwesterly by midday at 6 km/h (3 kt) with gusts to 16 km/h (9 kt), and finally turns west-northwesterly into the evening at 12 km/h (6 kt), gusting 17 km/h (9 kt). The peak gust across the gulf is 25 km/h (13 kt). Thunderstorm gust hazards are possible when thunder develops, potentially exceeding these values.

## Detailed Discussion

### Synoptic Overview

Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the north (1007 hPa) and highest toward the northeast (1014 hPa), creating a moderate large-scale gradient. Basin pressure today averages between 1011.1 and 1013.2 hPa and is near-steady, with a slight rise of +0.8 hPa in the latest call. The lower pressure lies toward the north, indicating a gentle pressure push from that direction.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes

The review notes that at Day+0 no model is meaningfully better than the others, though GFS misses the thunderstorms and both GFS and ECMWF under-forecast peak wind. Best Match under-forecasts daytime highs and peak wind, while ECMWF also under-forecasts highs and wind. The Day+0 call aligns with the models on temperature and rain probability, but Best Match sits on the wrong side of its own rain record. KMD’s forecast matches the call on temperature but offers only a light-showers chance, lacking a thunder forecast. Data sufficiency is strong with 63 checks for Day+0, providing a settled picture despite uneven coverage for KMD.

Rain loses support through Sunday, from all four models Friday to two of four models Sunday. Sunday's call: rain, 54%, with two of four models wet; highs around 30°C (86°F). Kenya Meteorological Department (KMD) calls it dry. At this lead Best Match has the best record, right 87% of the time over 82 checks.

Further out, cooling through Thursday, with showers and thunderstorms likely Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday, and rain and thunderstorms possible Thursday. Monday: three of four models wet, highs 28 to 30°C (82 to 86°F). Tuesday: all four models wet, highs around 28°C (82°F). Wednesday: all three models that reach it wet, highs 26 to 29°C (80 to 84°F).

Only GFS, ECMWF and ICON reach past Tuesday. ICON and UKMO are the wetter solutions from Monday to Tuesday; GFS and ECMWF keep it drier. Thursday's call: rain, 100%, with both models wet; highs around 26°C (80°F). At this lead ECMWF has the best record, right 87% of the time over 78 checks.
